content:
You are a research assistant answering questions about a fixed set of papers.
The papers are plain-text files in your working directory. Explore them with the tools:
- bash: read-only shell (ls, grep -n, find, head, tail, wc, nl, cat, sed -n 'A,Bp')
- read(path, offset, limit): read a file with line numbers

Rules:
- Answer ONLY from text you have actually read in this session. Do not answer from memory.
- If the papers do not contain the answer, say so explicitly instead of guessing.
- When you have enough evidence, reply with your final answer and make NO tool call.
- Support every factual claim with a verbatim quote copied exactly from the source, in the form: "exact text" (file). Never paraphrase inside the quotation marks. A statement that the document(s) do not contain the requested information needs no citation.
- State only what the document(s) say. Do not add background knowledge, general advice, or your own
  conclusions. If the user asks for something the text only partly covers, answer the covered part
  and say plainly which part the document does not address.
- Do not expand abbreviations, name entities, or add details that the text itself does not give.
- Do not end with a summary that recombines earlier points ("In short", "Overall"); the points stand on their own.
- When the user describes their own situation, say what the document states that applies to it; do not
  draw a personal conclusion that the document does not state itself.
- After you give an answer, an automatic check verifies your citations. If you then receive a
  <verification> message, you are in revision mode: fix ONLY the flagged problems by calling
  edit_draft(old, new), where `old` is an exact, unique substring of your previous answer.
  Keep everything else unchanged, and reply "Done" when finished.
  Never call edit_draft before you have given an answer.

Summarize Section 1 in simple terms with a bullet point for each paragraph. Exclude the paragraph about the history of the section, and limit each bullet point to 30 words or less. Then, explain the importance of a pre-kindergarten program.

In your answer, refer only to the document in the file `doc.txt`. Do not employ any outside knowledge.

content:
1	SECTION 1. Public education.—
     2	 (a) The education of children is a fundamental value of the people of the State of Florida. It is,
     3	therefore, a paramount duty of the state to make adequate provision for the education of all
     4	children residing within its borders. Adequate provision shall be made by law for a uniform,
     5	efficient, safe, secure, and high quality system of free public schools that allows students to
     6	obtain a high quality education and for the establishment, maintenance, and operation of
     7	institutions of higher learning and other public education programs that the needs of the people may
     8	require. To assure that children attending public schools obtain a high quality education, the
     9	legislature shall make adequate provision to ensure that, by the beginning of the 2010 school year,
    10	there are a sufficient number of classrooms so that:
    11	 (1) The maximum number of students who are assigned to each teacher who is teaching in public
    12	school classrooms for prekindergarten through grade 3 does not exceed 18 students;
    13	 (2) The maximum number of students who are assigned to each teacher who is teaching in public
    14	school classrooms for grades 4 through 8 does not exceed 22 students; and
    15	 (3) The maximum number of students who are assigned to each teacher who is teaching in public
    16	school classrooms for grades 9 through 12 does not exceed 25 students.
    17	 The class size requirements of this subsection do not apply to extracurricular classes. Payment of
    18	the costs associated with reducing class size to meet these requirements is the responsibility of
    19	the state and not of local schools districts. Beginning with the 2003-2004 fiscal year, the
    20	legislature shall provide sufficient funds to reduce the average number of students in each
    21	classroom by at least two students per year until the maximum number of students per classroom does
    22	not exceed the requirements of this subsection.
    23	 (b) Every four-year old child in Florida shall be provided by the State a high quality
    24	pre-kindergarten learning opportunity in the form of an early childhood development and education
    25	program which shall be voluntary, high quality, free, and delivered according to professionally
    26	accepted standards. An early childhood development and education program means an organized program
    27	designed to address and enhance each child’s ability to make age appropriate progress in an
    28	appropriate range of settings in the development of language and cognitive capabilities and
    29	emotional, social, regulatory and moral capacities through education in basic skills and such other
    30	skills as the Legislature may determine to be appropriate.
    31	 (c) The early childhood education and development programs provided by reason of subparagraph (b)
    32	shall be implemented no later than the beginning of the 2005 school year through funds generated in
    33	addition to those used for existing education, health, and development programs. Existing education,
    34	health, and development programs are those funded by the State as of January 1, 2002 that provided
    35	for child or adult education, health care, or development.
    36	 History.—Am. proposed by Constitution Revision Commission, Revision No. 6, 1998, filed with the
    37	Secretary of State May 5, 1998; adopted 1998; Ams. by Initiative Petitions filed with the Secretary
    38	of State April 13, 2001, and January 25, 2002; adopted 2002.
    39	 SECTION 2. State board of education.—The state board of education shall be a body corporate and
    40	have such supervision of the system of free public education as is provided by law. The state board
    41	of education shall consist of seven members appointed by the governor to staggered 4-year terms,
    42	subject to confirmation by the senate. The state board of education shall appoint the commissioner
    43	of education.
    44	 History.—Am. proposed by Constitution Revision Commission, Revision No. 8, 1998, filed with the
    45	Secretary of State May 5, 1998; adopted 1998.
    46	 SECTION 3. Terms of appointive board members.—Members of any appointive board dealing with
    47	education may serve terms in excess of four years as provided by law.
    48	 SECTION 4. School districts; school boards.—
    49	 (a) Each county shall constitute a school district; provided, two or more contiguous counties, upon
    50	vote of the electors of each county pursuant to law, may be combined into one school district. In
    51	each school district there shall be a school board composed of five or more members chosen by vote
    52	of the electors in a nonpartisan election for appropriately staggered terms of four years, as
    53	provided by law.
    54	 (b) The school board shall operate, control and supervise all free public schools within the school
    55	district and determine the rate of school district taxes within the limits prescribed herein. Two or
    56	more school districts may operate and finance joint educational programs.
    57	 History.—Am. proposed by Constitution Revision Commission, Revision No. 11, 1998, filed with the
    58	Secretary of State May 5, 1998; adopted 1998.
    59	 SECTION 5. Superintendent of schools.—In each school district there shall be a superintendent of
    60	schools who shall be elected at the general election in each year the number of which is a multiple
    61	of four for a term of four years; or, when provided by resolution of the district school board, or
    62	by special law, approved by vote of the electors, the district school superintendent in any school
    63	district shall be employed by the district school board as provided by general law. The resolution
    64	or special law may be rescinded or repealed by either procedure after four years.
    65	 History.—Am. proposed by Constitution Revision Commission, Revision No. 13, 1998, filed with the
    66	Secretary of State May 5, 1998; adopted 1998.
    67	 SECTION 6. State school fund.—The income derived from the state school fund shall, and the
    68	principal of the fund may, be appropriated, but only to the support and maintenance of free public
    69	schools.
    70	 SECTION 7. State University System.—
    71	 (a) PURPOSES. In order to achieve excellence through teaching students, advancing research and
    72	providing public service for the benefit of Florida’s citizens, their communities and economies, the
    73	people hereby establish a system of governance for the state university system of Florida.
    74	 (b) STATE UNIVERSITY SYSTEM. There shall be a single state university system comprised of all
    75	public universities. A board of trustees shall administer each public university and a board of
    76	governors shall govern the state university system.
    77	 (c) LOCAL BOARDS OF TRUSTEES. Each local constituent university shall be administered by a board of
    78	trustees consisting of thirteen members dedicated to the purposes of the state university system.
    79	The board of governors shall establish the powers and duties of the boards of trustees. Each board
    80	of trustees shall consist of six citizen members appointed by the governor and five citizen members
    81	appointed by the board of governors. The appointed members shall be confirmed by the senate and
    82	serve staggered terms of five years as provided by law. The chair of the faculty senate, or the
    83	equivalent, and the president of the student body of the university shall also be members.

**Section 1 summary (one bullet per paragraph, history paragraph excluded):**

- The state must provide a uniform, efficient, safe, secure, high-quality free public school system, with class sizes capped at 18 (pre-K–3), 22 (4–8), and 25 (9–12) students per teacher.
- Every four-year-old in Florida must be offered a voluntary, free, high-quality pre-kindergarten program delivered according to professionally accepted standards.
- The program must start no later than the 2005 school year, funded with money added to existing education, health, and development programs.

**Importance of the pre-kindergarten program:**

According to the document, the program matters because it is "designed to address and enhance each child's ability to make age appropriate progress ... in the development of language and cognitive capabilities and emotional, social, regulatory and moral capacities through education in basic skills" (doc.txt). In other words, its importance is that it helps each child develop language, thinking, and emotional, social, and moral abilities at an age-appropriate level.
